---
title: "Using recipes in scikit-learn pipelines"
toc: true
---

A `shoez` recipe handles feature engineering; the model that consumes those
features lives downstream in [scikit-learn](https://scikit-learn.org/). The
`RecipeTransformer` adapter bridges the two: it wraps a recipe so it behaves
like any other scikit-learn transformer and drops straight into a
`sklearn.pipeline.Pipeline`.

## The adapter

`RecipeTransformer` wraps an *unfitted* recipe. It exposes the familiar
scikit-learn `fit` / `transform` / `fit_transform` methods, so the recipe's
`specify → fit → transform` lifecycle is driven by the pipeline rather than by
hand.

```{python}
from sklearn.datasets import load_breast_cancer

X, y = load_breast_cancer(return_X_y=True, as_frame=True)
X.iloc[:5, :3]
```

scikit-learn keeps the features `X` and the target `y` apart, while `shoez`
identifies the outcome by its **role**. Build the recipe with the outcome role
assigned; the adapter re-joins `y` onto `X` under that name at fit time and
strips it back out of the transformed output, so `transform` returns the feature
matrix only.

```{python}
from shoez import Recipe, StepNormalize

features = list(X.columns)

recipe = (
    Recipe(data=X.assign(target=y))
    .set_roles(outcome="target", predictor=features)
    .add(StepNormalize(features))
)
```

## Inside a `Pipeline`

Wrap the recipe in `RecipeTransformer` and place it ahead of an estimator. The
pipeline's `fit` flows `X`/`y` through the recipe, then fits the model on the
engineered features:

```{python}
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline

from shoez import RecipeTransformer

pipe = Pipeline(
    [
        ("recipe", RecipeTransformer(recipe)),
        ("model", LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000)),
    ]
)
pipe.fit(X, y)
pipe.score(X, y)
```

## Cross-validation and tuning

Because the adapter stores the recipe verbatim, it clones cleanly — so it works
inside `GridSearchCV` and any other tool that re-fits across folds:

```{python}
from sklearn.model_selection import GridSearchCV

search = GridSearchCV(pipe, {"model__C": [0.1, 1.0]}, cv=3)
search.fit(X, y)
search.best_params_
```

## Feature names and `set_output`

`RecipeTransformer` implements `get_feature_names_out`, so it composes inside a
`ColumnTransformer` and supports the `set_output` API for choosing the container
type returned by `transform`:

```{python}
rt = RecipeTransformer(recipe).set_output(transform="pandas")
rt.fit(X, y).transform(X).iloc[:5, :3]
```
